Marketing & reviews tools for Roofers

Tools that help roofers with marketing & reviews. Getting found locally, collecting reviews, and producing content without a marketing team.

Where Marketing & reviews goes wrong for Roofers

Storm damage drives most roofing leads, and the first company to inspect usually wins. Reviews carrying photos of completed roofs do more than any paid listing.

What Roofers jobs really involve

Roofing jobs are high value, weather dependent and frequently disputed, which makes photo documentation and written scope unusually important. Much of the work is also sold through inspections and insurance claims, so records carry real weight.

Frequently asked questions

Which marketing & reviews tools work best for roofers?

The three that fit best here are Podium (Businesses where most enquiries arrive by text or webchat), Structurely (Contractors with long sales cycles who lose leads to slow follow-up), Birdeye (Businesses that depend on local search and online reviews). Start with the one whose description matches your crew size, not the one with the longest feature list.

How much does marketing & reviews software cost for roofers?

Across the 6 tools on this page, 2 have a free tier and the rest are paid, most of them billed per user per month. Prices change often, so treat the figures here as indicative and confirm on the vendor site.

Why does marketing & reviews cause problems for roofers specifically?

Storm damage drives most roofing leads, and the first company to inspect usually wins. Reviews carrying photos of completed roofs do more than any paid listing.

How do I price weather risk into a roofing quote?

Most roofers price the job normally and manage weather through scheduling, with a clause covering delays. Adding a large contingency to the number usually just loses the job.
